Tagging reference

Type brackets round the words

  • [gaffer tape]→gaffer tapeProp
  • {kitchen}→kitchenLocation
  • ~lens flare~→lens flareVFX
  • <tripod>→tripodGear

The tag is made the moment you type the closing bracket.

Or type its name and a colon, then Tab

In the Visual column: VFX: glow Tab tags glow as VFX.

  • Prop:→gaffer tapeProp
  • Location: Loc:→kitchenLocation
  • Cast:→MayaCast
  • VFX:→glowVFX
  • Gear:→tripodGear
  • SFX: Music:→rain ambienceMusic/SFX

Any capitals work. Esc cancels, and Ctrl+Z after Tab undoes just the tag and leaves the plain text.

Or select the words and press Tag

  • Select + Tag→any category, in either column

Keys

  • Tabcompletes a tag you've already used, in its own category
  • CtrlEnterstarts the next scene and jumps into it
  • CtrlFfind and replace across the whole script

Click a tag in the script, or its card in Production, to say who's responsible and keep notes, links or file paths against it.

    Splitpage

    Splitpage is a two-column script editor for video: what the viewer sees on the left, what gets said on the right. It has a teleprompter, comments, and a production breakdown that tracks every prop, location, VFX shot and person in the script.

    Scripts save as plain Markdown (.md) you can open anywhere, or as .splitpage files. Splitpage runs in a browser or as a desktop app for Windows.

    What's new in the 4.0 beta

    • No new features; sturdier saving. 4.0 rebuilds the inside of Splitpage. Your 3.1 scripts and files open as before.
    • Saving and switching scripts is safer. A save, paste, drop, thumbnail, annotation, history restore or draft restore that finishes after you opened or reopened another script no longer lands in it. A failed save no longer changes the next script's revision, and saves to one place wait for each other. A paste or drop that was too late says the picture was not added.
    • Exports are built from the script as you chose them. Edits made while an export is prepared no longer change it.
    • Damaged files open or merge instead of failing. A file whose top level is not a script counts as no document; odd scenes, comments, people, tags, shots and reply times are dropped or ignored.
    • Editing. No edit leaves half an emoji; names cut at their limit keep whole characters. A cancelled IME composition leaves no empty Undo step. A split or join in the writer refreshes Production and B-roll. If drawing the screen fails, the previous picture stays.
    • Production. A tag name of only invisible characters is refused. Deleting a person clears them as owner of their b-roll shots at once. Gear quick add and tag suggestions handle names such as constructor. Drawing the b-roll badge no longer creates or renames shots.
    • Pasting deeply nested formatting around many links can no longer produce a huge result.
    • At 1440 px with a long title focused, the search button and the identity chip no longer overlap.
    • In the desktop app, some menu-bar commands ran behind an open dialog, the writer or Present. They now stop and say what to close first: Save and Save As… (Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Shift+S) while a dialog or the command menu is open; Open… (Ctrl+O) and Export… while either of those, the writer or Present is; Find & replace while a dialog or the writer is; Hide shot scenes (Ctrl+Alt+H) while a dialog is. Search Commands… already stopped under a dialog, the writer, Present or the tour, and now says why too.
    • In the desktop app, more menu-bar commands ran behind the writer, Present, the B-roll shot list page or the tour. They now stop and say what to close first: Present, Write, Production (Ctrl+Alt+P), Gear, Comments (Ctrl+Alt+C) and Version history… while a dialog, the command menu, the writer, Present, the shot list or the tour is open (Present and Write not for themselves); Open… (Ctrl+O), Export… (Ctrl+E), Search Commands… (Ctrl+K) and Find & replace (Ctrl+F) also while the shot list or the tour is, and Find & replace while Present is; Save to file, Present in Browser (Ctrl+Shift+P), Use Chromium Speech Recognition and each File ▸ Export format while a dialog or the command menu is.
    • In the desktop app, a menu-bar command that opens a dialog opened it underneath the tour, or on top of a dialog that was already open. About Splitpage, Settings…, Paste a script…, Import from Google Doc link…, Set up Splitpage… and Tagging reference now stop and say what to close first while the tour or a dialog is open. User guide… (F1) still opens during the tour, but not over another dialog.
    • Ctrl+Z right after opening writer mode closes writer instead of undoing a change hidden behind it in the split view. Ctrl+Shift+Z brings writer back.
    • Merging two versions of a script could drop, duplicate or keep a deleted scene, comment, crew member, breakdown entry or b-roll shot whose id was a special word such as constructor or __proto__, and could blank a scene's text. Only a hand-edited or damaged file has such ids. They now merge like any other, and files that have them open unchanged.
    • A scene, comment or person whose id was a special word such as constructor also tripped up undo, Hide shot scenes, comments, Find and the Production panel: undoing the delete of such a scene could fail, and such a shot scene never hid. They now behave like any other.
    • When a merge found that you and someone else had both added the same person, the production items and b-roll shots you had given that person came out unassigned. They now keep that person as their owner.
    • Commenting a b-roll key's line no longer moves the comment off the key or gives the shot a new id.
    • Words marked as both a comment and a production tag or b-roll key in one piece of markup, as a script or paste from elsewhere can carry them, kept the tag or key but lost the comment's highlight, leaving its card "No longer in script". Both are now kept.
    • A comment on a stage direction or a sound cue, in a script or paste that carries both marks on the same words in one piece of markup, kept the comment but lost the direction or cue mark. Both are now kept.
    • Markdown export wrote [text](null) for a link with no address. It now writes the text alone.
    • Deleting one SFX: or Music: cue and editing another in the same cell at once could hand the deleted cue's Production item, with its status and notes, to the edited cue, and leave the edited cue's own item "Not in script". The edited cue now keeps its own item when its new words are close to its old ones and to no other cue that went. When that can't be told, it gets a new item at Needed and both old items stay, "Not in script", rather than the wrong one being renamed.
    • Fixed: when one edit to a cell's sound cues lost a cue, added another and changed a third, the changed cue's item could be renamed to the wrong name. Cues are now matched to their old names by how alike they are, and when that is unclear they get a new item instead. Find-and-replace across several cues in one cell no longer renames their items.
    • Saving while a script was still opening, with Save in the header or in the desktop app's menu bar (Ctrl+S), did nothing and reported an error in the background. It now says "Still loading…", as the File menu's commands already did.
    • In Present, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+M, Alt+F and the like flipped or mirrored the text, and Ctrl, Cmd or Alt with Space still played or paused it. M, F and Space now do nothing in Present while Ctrl, Cmd or Alt is held, none of Present's keys act while you type in a field such as the Find box, and pressing M or F with the caret still in a script cell no longer types the letter into it.
    • An emoji no longer breaks in two when a tag name cut inside it is tagged with "Tag all mentions", or when text is pasted, cut or split at a position inside it.
    • Pasted or imported text with a link inside another link could lose text the next time it was saved, merged or pasted. The inner link now keeps its own address and the outer link continues around it, as when you set a link inside a link in the editor, and a video card inside a link stays a card.

    What's new in 3.1

    • Collaborate. Collab in the header (or File ▸ Collaborate…) puts the script on your server and gives you two links to send: one to edit, one to comment. A link opens that one script, needs no account, and can be renewed or turned off.
    • Unsaved changes to a server script survive a closed tab. The browser keeps them as you type and merges them back in the next time you open the script, with Undo merge.
    • Draw on your pictures. In a scene's gallery, press Annotate to mark up a picture with a pen, a highlighter, text and an eraser (P, H, T and E pick them). Your marks stay editable, and Remove annotations gives you the original back. See Annotating a picture.
    • Search commands (Ctrl+K) puts the tagging reference first, and searching tags finds it.
    • Export to Excel. File ▸ Export… ▸ Spreadsheet now makes an Excel workbook: sized columns, wrapped text, a frozen header with filters, a Notes column to write in, and a sheet for each part. CSV is the second choice on the same card, and the Breakdown and the B-roll shot list offer both. See Exporting.
    • The writer's tools are at the top, under the title, where the script's formatting bar is, and Close is beside Save.
    • The tagging reference lists every word form: Prop:, Location: or Loc:, Cast:, VFX:, Gear:, and SFX: or Music:, each with its tag colour, beside the bracket shortcuts.
    • Saving you can trust. Text typed while a save is still going stays marked unsaved until it is saved, instead of being called saved.
    • An empty scene deletes in one click: its ⋯ ▸ Delete no longer asks twice when there is nothing in it to lose.
    • Version history from 2.x is no longer converted. If you are updating straight from 2.x, install 3.0 first to keep it. Nothing changes if you already have 3.0.

    What's new in 3.0

    • A new look. Calmer dark and light themes, a running order of the whole script under the header, each scene's status as a lamp, and side panels that open beside the script instead of over it.
    • A start screen for every new tab: a blank script, three starter scripts, a long demo that shows off every feature, your recent documents and a drop zone for a file.
    • One undo for everything. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z take back typing, tags, scene moves, statuses, pictures, comments and Production changes.
    • Stage directions: type ((beat)) in the Audio column.
    • Sound cues: start an Audio line with SFX: or Music:.
    • Timing: set a target length for the piece, or a scene's length by hand.
    • Several pictures and videos per scene, with YouTube, Vimeo and dropped video files playing in the scene's gallery. Click a picture to see it full size.
    • Settings in one place (File ▸ Settings), script zoom (Ctrl + mouse wheel), Search commands (Ctrl+K) and one Export dialog (Ctrl+E).
    • A B-roll panel built for the shoot, with prop statuses and a full-page shot list.
    • Exports that match the app: the PDF and Word script carry each scene's status, timecode and read time, tags in their colours, numbered comments, the breakdown and a b-roll shot list. Markdown and spreadsheets gain the same, and the packing list has sign-off lines.
    • Merging a word at a time: two people's edits to one scene combine unless they changed the same words.
    • Plain-language tags: type VFX: or Prop: in the Visual column and press Tab. The tagging reference is now a card that floats beside you.
    • Tag every mention at once: find a word (Ctrl+F) and press Tag all as….
    • Whole scenes: drag out of a text box to select scenes, then copy, cut, paste or delete them, comments and pictures included.
    • The rundown magnifies the scenes under the pointer, shows the script's length at its end.
    • In the desktop app: Follow My Voice through Windows' own speech recognition.

    Release notes for every version are on the releases page.

    Getting started

    • Setup. The first time you open a fresh copy, a short wizard asks how you'll be working and offers the tour. File ▸ Set up reopens it any time; it never changes your script.
    • The tour. File ▸ Tour walks through five things to know, each with a Read more link into this guide.
    • Help. File ▸ Help opens this guide (F1 in the desktop app).

    The start screen

    A new tab opens on a start screen rather than a document. The browser app shows it too, on a fresh copy nothing has been opened in.

    • Blank script: one empty scene.
    • Starter scripts: To-camera video, Interview and 30-second spot. Each opens as a new, unsaved script to write over.
    • Open a file, or drop a .md, .splitpage, .docx, .txt or .csv file anywhere on the page. The drop zone's links paste a script or import a Google Doc link.
    • Recent (desktop app): the last 20 documents you had open. Click one to reopen it; × takes it off the list, Clear recent empties it. Continue at the top reopens the most recent.
    • Take the tour, or Look at the example script (or Esc) to close the start screen and see the demo script.
    • Open the long demo (30 scenes): a whole video, nearly ten minutes long, with every feature in use (all three scene statuses, every tag category, b-roll, comments, stage directions, set read times and a target length), to see how Splitpage handles a real-length script. Like a starter, it opens as a new, unsaved copy. The command menu (Ctrl+K) opens it too, keeping the script you had in Version history.

    Running it

    Desktop app: install it from the releases page (see Installing and updating).

    Portable copy, in a browser: unzip splitpage-<version>.zip anywhere and double-click index.html. Writing, comments, the teleprompter and export all work straight away. To install it as an app and use it offline, serve it instead:

    1. Run start.bat (Windows), ./start.sh (macOS or Linux) or node start.mjs. It opens http://localhost:8791/ in your browser.
    2. In Chrome or Edge, click the install icon in the address bar to give Splitpage its own window and a Start Menu entry.
    3. Keep the launcher running while you work: closing it stops the server. Your scripts are ordinary files and don't depend on it.

    The launcher needs Node. Without it, open index.html directly.

    Writing and planning

    Each scene is a row: Visual on the left, Audio on the right.

    • Format text: select words and use the toolbar: bold (Ctrl+B), italic (Ctrl+I), underline (Ctrl+U), strikethrough, highlight, link, comment and tag.
    • New scene: Ctrl+Enter starts the next scene and moves into it.
    • Split a scene: Alt+Enter moves everything after the caret into a new scene below, in the same column.
    • Move a scene: Alt+↑ / Alt+↓, or drag it by its number. The scene's ⋯ menu also has Move up, Move down, Insert scene and Delete. Delete asks for a second click, unless the scene is empty (no words, pictures, set length or comments): then one click does it. Ctrl+Z brings a deleted scene back.
    • The rundown: the strip under the header shows every scene as a block. Hover it to magnify the scenes round the pointer, click a block to jump to that scene, or drop a dragged scene on it to move the scene. File ▸ Minimise the rundown shrinks it to a line; click the line to bring it back.
    • The header's buttons: Production, Gear, B-roll and Comments open their panels; Write and Present are the two other ways to see it. In a narrower window the panel buttons shrink to their icons and counts, and Write to its icon. Point at one, Comments open their panels; Write and Present are the two other ways to see it. In a narrower window the panel buttons shrink to their icons and counts, and Write to its icon. Point at one, or Tab to it, and its name slides out over its neighbours.
    • Scene status: click the lamp in the scene's gutter to cycle To do → Ready → Shot.
    • Hide shot scenes: File ▸ Hide shot scenes (Ctrl+Alt+H) collapses Shot scenes into a thin strip. Click the strip to see them.
    • Undo and redo: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z (or Ctrl+Y) work on the whole script from anywhere in it. Someone else's merged changes are never undone.
    • Find and replace: Ctrl+F. Enter and Shift+Enter step through matches; Aa matches case. Tagged words are skipped; when that's the only place a word appears, the count says so ("No matches · 1 in a tag"). Rename those in Production.
    • Tag every mention at once: in the find bar, Tag all as… tags every whole-word mention of the search in the Visual column as one category — find "drone", pick Gear, and all of them are tagged. It shows the count before it runs, leaves mentions that are already tagged, and one Ctrl+Z undoes the whole batch.
    • Zoom the script: Ctrl + mouse wheel (or pinch) over the script, or Ctrl++ / − / 0. Only the script changes size, from 70 % to 200 %. Click the size note to go back to 100 %.

    On a Mac, read Cmd for Ctrl throughout.

    Timing

    Splitpage estimates each scene's read time from its Audio words, at the script's reading speed. Visual notes, stage directions and sound cues don't count.

    • Script length: the small time at the end of the rundown, just after the last scene (at the strip's right edge on a long script, and at the right of the status line on a phone). With shot scenes hidden it reads what's left / the whole script. It stays on the minimized rundown.
    • Reading speed: click the script length. It's saved with the script.
    • A scene's length by hand, for a montage, a title card or a pause: click the scene's time in the Read column, type 1:30, 90, 90s or 1m30, and press Enter. Clear it and press Enter to go back to the estimate. It turns amber if the words would take longer.
    • Target length: click the script length and pick or type a Target length (or search commands for target). The length then reads 4:32 / 5:00 · 0:28 left, or how far over in red. No target removes it.

    Whole scenes

    • Select: click in a text box and drag up or down past its edge. The page scrolls at the window's edge. Esc or a click lets go.
    • Ctrl+C copies, Ctrl+X cuts, Delete removes. Right-click for the same, plus New script from these scenes (it replaces this tab's script; the old one goes to Version history).
    • Paste with the caret in any script, in another tab or the desktop app too: the scenes go in after that scene, or replace it if it's empty, with their comments, status, b-roll, breakdown details and pictures (up to 16 MB of pictures per copy). One Ctrl+Z undoes it.
    • Into Word or Google Docs they paste as a two-column table.

    The writer

    Write in the header opens the Audio column as one flowing document, for when the job is writing narration. One paragraph is one scene. Its tools sit along the top, under the title, and Close (or Esc) is beside Save.

    • Enter starts a new scene, Shift+Enter is a line break, and Backspace at the start of a paragraph joins it to the one above.
    • The margin button cycles Visuals (each scene's visual, greyed; click it to jump there), Numbers and Compact.
    • Size sets the text size for you on this device, not in the script.
    • Tags, formatting and Save work as in the split view.
    • Two scenes that both have a visual can't be joined here. Join them in the split view.

    Stage directions

    A stage direction is a note for the reader, like (beat) or (look to camera 2), written into the Audio column where it applies.

    • Type ((beat)). The double brackets become a direction when you type the last one. Ctrl+Z straight after gives you the brackets back. Single brackets stay as you typed them.
    • Or select words and press ( ) on the Audio column's formatting bar or the writer's bar. Press it again to turn a direction back into words.

    Directions show dim and in brackets, appear in the teleprompter, are never waited for by Follow My Voice, and don't count toward the read time.

    Sound cues

    Start a line of the Audio column with SFX: or Music: (any case), and that whole line becomes a sound cue: SFX: door slam. It turns into one when you type the colon, and Ctrl+Z straight after gives you plain words back. Mid-sentence, SFX: is just words; in the Visual column it starts a Music/SFX tag instead.

    A cue is its own small line in the Music/SFX colour, with a note in front, so your eye skips it while reading. It is never on the teleprompter (a pause for the sound is a stage direction's job), doesn't count toward the read time, and is left out of the narration export. The script exports print it as its own line. Each cue is an item in the Production panel's Music & SFX list, named by the words after the colon (a tag or a stage direction on the line is not part of the name), with its own status and owner like any tag. Edit the cue's words and its item follows, keeping its status.

    Comments

    • Leave one: select text and press the comment button (the speech bubble) in the formatting toolbar. The words get a dotted underline and a number.
    • The Comments panel shows one card per thread. Click a card to jump to its words. Write a reply… replies, Resolve closes the thread, Assign hands it to someone, and ⋯ ▸ Delete deletes it.
    • Filter with the Open / Resolved / All tabs and the person menu, and sort by Script order or Most recent.

    Pictures and video

    • Add a picture: Add picture under a scene's Visual text, or drop an image file on the Visual column.
    • Paste or drop a picture, a video file or a video link (YouTube, Vimeo and the like) into a scene and it goes into that scene's Image section, with Undo on the notice. The words you pasted with it stay in the text.
    • Several per scene: the first is the cover, the next ones sit beside it, and +N stands for the rest. Videos are also listed underneath.
    • The gallery: click any tile. Use ‹ › or ← → to browse, Shift+← / → or drag to reorder, Make cover, Remove (Delete), and Esc to close.
    • See a picture at full size: click the big picture in the gallery (or press Enter on it). A large picture opens fitted to the window; click it or scroll to see it at 100 %, and drag to look around. ← → go through the scene's pictures, and Esc, × or a click outside goes back to the gallery.
    • Draw on a picture: pick it in the gallery and press Annotate. See Annotating a picture.
    • Watch a video: press ▶ in the gallery. YouTube and Vimeo links play there, and so does a video file dropped since you opened the script. Anything else opens with Open link / Open file.
    • Video thumbnails: pasting a YouTube or Vimeo link fetches its thumbnail once. Turn this off in Settings ▸ Fetch video thumbnails.
    • Comments can carry a picture too: the image button in the comment box.

    A saved file carries all its pictures. One that can't be found shows as Image unavailable; the rest of the script is fine.

    Annotating a picture

    Circle the thing that matters, highlight a corner, or write a note right on a picture. Open the scene's gallery, pick the picture and press Annotate. It opens over the whole window with the tools along the top:

    • Pen and Highlighter draw where you drag, with a mouse, a pen or a finger. The highlighter is wide and see-through.
    • Text: click the picture and type. Click away or press Esc to put it down. With Text picked, click a text to change it or drag it to move it.
    • Eraser: drag over a mark to take the whole mark away.
    • P, H, T and E pick the pen, highlighter, text and eraser (not while you're typing a text).
    • Six colours and three sizes (S, M, L). Changing them while you type changes the text you're typing.
    • Undo and Redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z) step through your marks, and Clear all takes them all away.
    • Done saves. Cancel or Esc leaves without saving; if you've drawn something it asks first, so press it again to throw the marks away.

    The scene shows the picture with your marks everywhere: the script, the exports and the teleprompter. The original is kept, so Edit annotations opens your marks again to change them, and Remove annotations puts the picture back as it was. Saving is one step of the script's undo, so Ctrl+Z afterwards takes it back too.

    Presenting

    Present in the header opens the teleprompter.

    • Space plays and pauses, ↑ / ↓ change the speed, and Esc closes it.
    • Follow My Voice scrolls as you read aloud.
    • Mirror (M) and Flip (F) are for a beam-splitter or an upside-down monitor.
    • Skip shot leaves out scenes marked Shot.
    • Scene mode plays one scene at a time and pauses at its end. The arrows (or ← / →) step between scenes.

    In the desktop app, Follow My Voice uses Windows' speech recognition; see Desktop app.

    Getting the narration out

    File ▸ Export… ▸ Narration only writes the Audio column as .docx or .txt, one paragraph per scene; the .docx puts each scene's number in the margin, so a session can pick up "from 14". Include stage directions puts them in as (beat). Sound cues are never in it. Paste a script… reads that shape back in.

    Tagging and the production breakdown

    Tag things in the script and they appear in the Production panel, with every scene they're in. While you type a tag you've used before, Tab accepts the completion Splitpage offers.

    The tagging reference: File ▸ Tagging reference (or search commands for it) opens a card at the bottom right of the script (a sheet at the bottom on a phone). It shows every way to type a tag, each in its tag colour: the brackets, and a category's name and a colon for all six categories. It stays while you scroll and type, fading while the caret is under it. Esc or × closes it. Cast and Music/SFX have no brackets: type Cast:, SFX: or Music:, or select the words and press Tag.

    Icons on tags: turn on Settings ▸ Show icons on tags to put a small icon before each tag as well as its colour: a box for a prop, a pin for a location, a person for cast, a sparkle for VFX, a note for music and sound, a camera for gear. It helps when the colours are hard to tell apart, for example in greyscale. The icons also show in the Production and Gear panels and on the tagging reference. They are never part of your text, so copying, exports and read times stay the same, and the teleprompter leaves them out.

    Plain-language tags: in the Visual column, type a category and a colon (VFX:, Prop:, Location: or Loc:, Cast:, Gear:, SFX: or Music:, in any case). The words you type next are tinted in that category's colour.

    • Tab (on a phone, tap the note under the box) makes them one tag.
    • Esc cancels and leaves the plain text.
    • Ctrl+Z after Tab takes the tag off and leaves your words as you typed them.

    The Production panel, grouped by category or person, is a table: Item · Status · Scenes · Owner. Click a scene number to jump to it.

    • Open an item: click its name, or the tag in the script. Set its Status, Assigned to (Add person adds a name), and Notes & links. ⋯ has Rename and Remove label / Delete from list.
    • Status: Needed → Sourcing → Have it → Returned. Click the status to step it on. "Returned" also means finished with, for a location or VFX shot.
    • Several at once: Ctrl+click items (Shift+click for a run) to assign, set status or delete them together. Deleting removes their tags from the script too; the words stay. Esc clears the selection.
    • Group by category, person or scene, or Shoot to see scenes grouped by location, with what each needs.
    • Untagged mentions: write the name of something already tracked in the Visual column without tagging it, and it gets a dotted underline and a Tag offer. Tab takes it, Esc waves it off. To tag them all at once, open the item and press Tag all N mentions.
    • Not in script: deleting a tag from the script keeps the item, flagged, until you delete it.
    • Export it with the panel's CSV button, or File ▸ Export… ▸ Breakdown. PDF, Word and Markdown exports include the breakdown too.

    Gear

    Gear in the header lists equipment: cameras, mics, lights. Gear that's never written in the script goes in the Add gear box at the foot of the panel, one item per line; press Update list. List or Scene changes the view. Packing list prints a checklist with a box for going out and one for coming back, and lines to sign.

    B-roll

    Start a line in the Visual column with B-roll: and it becomes a shot on the B-roll list. Lines under it, up to the next marker, are its description.

    • Mark a shot done: tick its box.
    • Filter with All / To shoot / Flagged / Shot, and group by scene or location.
    • Open a shot to set its location, who's getting it, its props, a note, or Flag for reshoot. ⋯ has Rename in script and Delete from list.
    • Props: a prop tagged in a shot's lines counts for it. Add others with Add prop.
    • Several at once: Ctrl+click or Shift+click shots, then mark, assign, move or flag them together.
    • Add a shot at the foot of the panel for one the script doesn't have.
    • The shot list: the arrows button beside the panel's × opens every shot on one page, grouped by location, scene or person, with CSV and Print shot list, which prints it as you see it there. ← Script or Esc goes back.

    Saving your script

    Save (Ctrl+S) writes the script to a file. The first Save asks where, and in which format:

    • Markdown (.md), the default: a readable table of scenes, then the breakdown and comments, then a block Splitpage keeps for itself (tags, comment anchors, pictures, statuses). Leave that block alone.
    • Splitpage (.splitpage): the same information without the readable table.

    Save a copy… (Ctrl+Shift+S) writes a new file and leaves the one on screen where it is.

    Autosave

    Once a script has a file, Splitpage writes each change to it a moment after you stop typing, and when you leave the window. Before the first Save, nothing is written. Turn it off with the Autosave switch at the top of the File menu.

    The Save button shows where things stand:

    • Saved just now for a minute after a write, then All changes saved for as long as nothing changes. Autosave still writes a couple of seconds after every change.
    • Saving… or Unsaved changes.
    • Not saving when something is in the way: the file changed on disk or a
    • Not saving when something is in the way: the file changed on disk, a write failed.

    Hover it for where and when ("Last saved to script.md at 2:52 PM") or what to do. The writer shows the same status.

    If you edit the .md somewhere else

    You can. Edit a cell in the table, save, and reopen it in Splitpage: your edit is kept, and tracked names in it are tagged again. A comment on words you rewrote loses its place. If you add or delete whole rows, Splitpage asks whether to keep its own record or rebuild the scenes from your table.

    If the file changes on disk while it's open here, Save offers Merge them, with a side-by-side view before anything is written. Where both versions changed the same words, the file's version goes in the script and yours is kept as an Unmerged edit comment.

    Sending it to someone

    • Nothing installed? File ▸ Export… ▸ SplitShare writes one .html file with the script and the whole app in it. It opens in any browser, on any device, with nothing to install, and they can read, edit and present it. It's a copy: their edits stay in their file. File ▸ Export… ▸ SplitShare writes one .html file with the script and the whole app in it. It opens in any browser, on any device, with nothing to install, and they can read, edit and present it. It's a copy: their edits stay in their file.

    Reopening a saved project

    • File ▸ Open… (Ctrl+O) opens a .md or .splitpage file with everything back: scenes, tags, comments, pictures.
    • A .docx, .txt, .csv or other Markdown file opens as a new script, with an empty breakdown and no comments.
    • A revised draft of the script you're in: use File ▸ Import ▸ Paste a script… instead. It replaces or appends the scenes and keeps this document's breakdown, cast, b-roll and comments. Paste text or Choose a file…. Tick Look for B-roll lines to track B-roll: lines.
    • A Google Doc: File ▸ Import ▸ Google Doc link… downloads it as a Word file in a new browser tab. Open that file with File ▸ Open….
    • An older .html project opens as it always did. The first Save asks where to keep it as .md; the .html file isn't touched.

    In Chrome or Edge, Splitpage reopens the last file you saved or opened when you start it on a fresh page. If the browser needs a click first, you'll see Continue where you left off?

    Version history

    File ▸ Version history… lists snapshots of the script as you worked. Pick one to restore it. Each script has its own history, kept on this computer (not in the file). History from older versions of Splitpage appears under Older history for 90 days. Only 3.0 carries history over from 2.x, so coming straight from 2.x, install 3.0 first to keep it.

    Exporting

    File ▸ Export… (Ctrl+E) opens one dialog for every format, with a preview and the file name.

    • The whole script: PDF, Word, Markdown, Spreadsheet (a row per scene, as Excel or CSV), or SplitShare (the script with the whole app built in, for any device).
    • Part of it: Narration only, the Breakdown as a spreadsheet, a Packing list of gear or props, or the B-roll shot list: a landscape table of every shot with its scene, props, flags and their reasons, and lines for notes (or the same as a spreadsheet).

    PDF and Word lay the script out the way the app does: the running time and target at the top (the PDF adds the rundown strip), each scene's number, start time, status and read time, tags in their colours, b-roll keys, and each open comment's number beside its words. At the end come the breakdown by category, the b-roll shot list and the numbered comments. The PDF's links can be clicked, and every page says "Page 2 of 8".

    Markdown comes in two shapes. Stacked reads like a script, one heading per scene with its start time, status and read time; with pictures it becomes a .zip with an images folder. Two columns is a table, Visual beside Audio, that Paste a script… can read back in. The Spreadsheet has a column each for start time, status, read time, tags, b-roll and open comments.

    Every spreadsheet — the script, the Breakdown and the B-roll shot list — comes two ways. Pick one under Format:

    • Excel (.xlsx) opens laid out and ready to read or print: columns sized to fit, long lines wrapped, the header row frozen with filters on it, a blank Notes column beside the scenes to write in, and a sheet each for the script, the comments, the breakdown and the b-roll (only the ones your script has). It opens in Excel, Google Sheets and Numbers.
    • CSV (.csv) is the plain values and nothing else, for another tool to read. Splitpage can open a CSV of the script again.

    Exports are copies to read, print or send. Opening one again brings back its scenes only, not the tags, comment anchors or statuses a saved file keeps. Export again in the File menu repeats the last format.

    The File menu

    Click the Splitpage mark at the top left (the file icon on a phone). At the top: where the script is saved and whether it's all saved (All changes saved · Markdown; hover for the time), the Autosave switch and Save a copy…. Below:

    • New & open: New script, Open…, Open recent (desktop app), and Import (Paste a script, Google Doc link).
    • Export: Export…, and Export again.
    • This document: Version history, Find & replace, Hide shot scenes, Minimise the rundown, and in the desktop app Present in browser and Use Chromium Speech Recognition.

    Settings, Help, Tour, Set up, About, Tagging reference and Export app data are along the bottom. An item that can't work right now says why.

    Search commands

    Press Ctrl+K, or click the search box in the header, and type part of what you want: pdf, gear, history, teleprompter. ↑ / ↓ choose, Enter runs, Esc closes. With nothing typed, your recent commands come first, then the tagging reference.

    Settings

    File ▸ Settings holds your preferences on this device. None of them change the script.

    • Appearance: theme, 12- or 24-hour clock (used for times such as the save status's "Last saved … at"), whether the rundown strip starts small, and Show icons on tags.
    • Editor: Hide shot scenes, Autosave, Fetch video thumbnails, the reading speed for new scripts, the writer's text size and script zoom.
    • Present: the teleprompter's Mirror, Flip and One scene at a time.
    • You: your name and colour. Clicking your name in the header opens these too.
    • You: your name and colour, which sign your edits and comments. Clicking your name in the header opens these too.
    • Help & tips: bring back the tagging reference, the tour and the desktop-app notice.
    • Data: Export app data.

    On a phone

    The whole app works on a phone, with the script first and scenes stacked (visual above audio).

    • The bar at the bottom opens Write, Production, Gear, B-roll and Comments; Script closes them. File and Present are at the top.
    • A scene's times show on the scene you're in.
    • Accept a tag completion: tap it (there's no Tab).
    • Find & replace and Search commands are in the File menu.
    • Select several breakdown items: long-press one, then tap others.
    • Move or add scenes from a scene's ⋯ menu, or + Add scene at the bottom.

    Desktop app

    The desktop app for Windows (x64 and ARM64) is Splitpage in its own window, with tabs, native Open and Save dialogs, and version history on disk. Double-clicking a .splitpage file opens it here.

    • Follow My Voice uses Windows' speech recognition, offline. Only one tab listens at a time. The status line names the microphone it's using. If it hears nothing, check, in Windows Settings:
      • System ▸ Sound: the default input is the right microphone.
      • Privacy & security ▸ Microphone: desktop apps may use it.
      • Time & language ▸ Speech: a recogniser for your language is installed.
    • Present in browser (File menu, Ctrl+Shift+P) opens a read-only teleprompter in your default browser, any browser, with the desktop app doing the listening. Save the script first. Use Chromium Speech Recognition opens it in Edge or Chrome to use that browser's recognition instead.
    • Crash recovery: unsaved changes are kept as you type and offered back, tab by tab, at the next launch.
    • Closing with unsaved work asks first. With several unsaved tabs, one dialog lists them all, with Review to go through them.

    Tabs

    • Ctrl+T opens a tab, on the start screen.
    • Ctrl+W or a middle-click closes one.
    • Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab switch tabs.
    • Drag a tab out to give it its own window, into another window to move it, or along the bar to reorder.

    Your tabs come back next time you launch Splitpage.

    Moving between the browser app and the desktop app

    File ▸ Export app data… saves your version history and preferences as a .json file. In the desktop app, File ▸ Import app data… merges one in; nothing is overwritten. Scripts themselves aren't included (they're your files). File ▸ Export app data… saves your version history and preferences as a .json file. In the desktop app, File ▸ Import app data… merges one in; nothing is overwritten. Scripts themselves aren't included (they're your files).

    Installing and updating

    • Desktop app: download SplitpageDesktopSetup-<version>-x64.exe (or -arm64.exe for Windows on ARM) from the releases page. It installs for you only, with no administrator needed. Windows may warn that it isn't signed: click More info ▸ Run anyway. If Splitpage is open with unsaved changes, it asks whether to save first, and Setup waits. If you choose Stay, save or close Splitpage yourself, then press Retry in Setup (or Cancel to install later).
    • Updates: when there's a newer version, a bar says so. In the desktop app, press Download, then Install and restart. A portable copy doesn't update itself: Open release page, then unzip the new release over the old folder.
    • Uninstalling: remove the desktop app in Windows' Installed apps. A portable copy is just a folder: delete it, after saving anything in its data folder you want to keep.

    Set up Splitpage

    Splitpage is a two-column visual/audio script editor with a built-in teleprompter. Scripts save as readable Markdown (.md) files by default — a table you can read and edit in any editor, with what Splitpage needs kept alongside it. You can also save as .splitpage, Splitpage's own format, if you would rather keep everything in one file.

    That's it — Splitpage saves your scripts as Markdown files you keep wherever you like, and everything above is always reachable again from File ▸ Set up Splitpage….
